lost_property.name: Lost Property
lost_property.description: The book at Castle Halt lists three things lost on the station road, the one I walked from the platform to Julie's. A red glove at the well, a felt hat at the signpost, and a dinner tin by the cart, further along toward Julie's gate. All three are at the roadside.
lost_property.completion: I entered all three. Each line already had a date of return pencilled beside it, and all three dates are next Sunday.
lost_property.returnTo: the lost-property book, on the platform at Castle Halt

requirements.text: A red glove, at the well on the station road
A felt hat, at the signpost on the station road
A dinner tin, by the cart on the station road

left_luggage.name: Left Luggage
left_luggage.description: A tin-lined trunk from the Goldskin Mining Co. has stood on the platform since it missed its train. The key went with the carter, last seen on the mine road with a full cart, near enough the mine to see it. The book doesn't say why he wasn't riding.
left_luggage.completion: Straw, and under it a gilder's book: tissue leaves with gold between them. Every leaf has been used but one. The consignment note gives the trunk's weight full, and it's the weight of the trunk empty.
left_luggage.returnTo: the trunk, on the platform at Castle Halt

requirements.text: The carter's cart, on the mine road near the mine
Open the trunk on the platform at Castle Halt

to_be_collected.name: To Be Collected
to_be_collected.description: A pencilled entry in the book says a parcel is left by the platform crate each evening after the bell, that it isn't lost property, and that it's always collected. It doesn't say who leaves it. It asks that someone check it's still being collected.
to_be_collected.completion: There was a parcel on the crate. Brown paper, string, no label. It was warm. I'd been watching the platform the whole time and I didn't see it put there.
to_be_collected.returnTo: the lost-property book, on the platform at Castle Halt

requirements.text: The platform at Castle Halt, after the nine o'clock bell

rats_in_the_sheds.name: Rats in the Sheds
rats_in_the_sheds.description: The Castle Allotment Society's notice says it has rats in its sheds and asks members to deal with any they see. Six would be a start. The plots are out past the last house, down the cinder path where the fingerpost says ALLOTMENTS. The notice adds that they did not use to be this size, and doesn't say since when.
rats_in_the_sheds.completion: Six. The sheds are quiet. Nothing in them had been eaten, and the seed drawers were all open and all full.
rats_in_the_sheds.returnTo: the parish board, in Castle square

requirements.text: Rats, in the allotments out past the last house

plot_nine.name: Plot 9
plot_nine.description: Plot 9 of the Castle allotments isn't let, and is freshly dug every morning. It's the plot with no name on the stake. The Society's notice would like someone to have a word with whoever it is, after nine presumably, and asks that the word be a quiet one.
plot_nine.completion: He had a good coat and his own spade, and he wasn't digging anything up. A hand's depth down in Plot 9 there's a jar with Julie's label, buried lid upward, carefully.
plot_nine.returnTo: the parish board, in Castle square

requirements.text: Whoever digs Plot 9, in the allotments, after the bell

three_scarecrows.name: Three Scarecrows
three_scarecrows.description: The farmer wants his three scarecrows counted while it's light: the one on the road by his gate, the one in the Long Hedge, and the one on the rim of the Top Field. He wouldn't open the door, and he wouldn't say what number he's hoping for.
three_scarecrows.completion: Three, by daylight. He thanked me through the door. There was a bag of apples on the step that hadn't been there when I knocked.
three_scarecrows.returnTo: the farmhouse door at Lowfield Farm

requirements.text: The scarecrow on the road by the farm gate
The scarecrow in the Long Hedge, off the footpath
The scarecrow on the rim of the Top Field, up the farm track

after_the_bell.name: After the Bell
after_the_bell.description: The farmer wants the same three scarecrows counted again after nine: the gate, the Long Hedge, the rim of the Top Field. He said to touch the rim and come straight back, and that he'd understand if I'd rather not. He said he'd rather not.
after_the_bell.completion: Three, after dark as well. He was quiet for a while behind the door. Then he said I'd have told him if it were four.
after_the_bell.returnTo: the farmhouse door at Lowfield Farm

requirements.text: The scarecrow by the farm gate, after the bell
The scarecrow in the Long Hedge, after the bell
The rim of the Top Field, up the farm track, after the bell

not_turnips.name: Not Turnips
not_turnips.description: The farmer planted turnips in the Top Field, the one up the farm track with the drills turned in it. From the upstairs window he counts six of something else, nearer the yard than they were on Sunday. He said there's nobody else to ask.
not_turnips.completion: Six. Cut, they're only pumpkins, hollow, with nothing in them. There's no seed in any of the six.
not_turnips.returnTo: the farmhouse door at Lowfield Farm

requirements.text: The things in the Top Field, up the farm track, in daylight

the_nurses_round.name: The Nurse's Round
the_nurses_round.description: A district nurse left her car in the wood with three visits still unticked on her list: Mrs Allen at Sallow Bottom, Mr Pike by the Long Hedge, the Misses Crane under Quarry Steps. All three cottages are on a road. The list says Tuesday. It doesn't say which.
the_nurses_round.completion: Three calls and nobody seen. One gone to town, one who wouldn't answer after nine, one step with eleven parcels on it. I ticked all three on her list.
the_nurses_round.returnTo: the glovebox of the car in the wood

requirements.text: Mrs Allen's cottage, on the road by Sallow Bottom
Mr Pike's cottage, on the road by the Long Hedge
The Misses Crane, on the road under Quarry Steps

her_coat.name: Her Coat
her_coat.description: The nurse's case is on the ground by the car, locked. Her coat isn't in the car. A woman's prints lead off behind it into the wood, and they aren't hurried. Her second note says not to come and look, and that she means it kindly.
her_coat.completion: The case opened. Dressings, a thermometer, a parcel made up for Mrs Allen. Everything in its place. Nothing in it had been used.
her_coat.returnTo: the nurse's case, in the car in the wood

requirements.text: Her coat, at the end of her prints into the wood behind the car
Her case, on the ground by the car

mrs_allens_dressing.name: Mrs Allen's Dressing
mrs_allens_dressing.description: There's a parcel in the nurse's case made up for Mrs Allen, who has gone to her sister's in Castle till it passes. Her note said the door facing the fire in the square. It didn't say what it is that will pass.
mrs_allens_dressing.completion: She wouldn't open the door. The parcel went in through the flap and a jar came out the same way, with Julie's writing on the lid.
mrs_allens_dressing.returnTo: Mrs Allen's sister's door, facing the fire in Castle square

requirements.text: The parcel, to the door facing the fire in Castle square

number_fourteen.name: No. 14
number_fourteen.description: A stone by the last lit lamp remembers A. Pell, lampman, who went out from it to see to No. 14. The dead lamps beyond it have numbers on them. By day there's no telling a dead lamp from a live one, so it will have to be after the bell.
number_fourteen.completion: I walked out past 12, 13 and 15 in the dark, came back to the last lit lamp, and told the stone what I'd counted.
number_fourteen.returnTo: Pell's stone, by the last lit lamp

requirements.text: No. 12, the first dark lamp past Pell's stone, at night
No. 13, the next lamp past Pell's stone, at night
No. 15, the last dark lamp past Pell's stone, at night

the_lampmans_brazier.name: The Lampman's Brazier
the_lampmans_brazier.description: A parish notice under Pell's stone says the lampman's brazier stands on the same road past No. 15, and is to be kept laid: two planks and a fire stone. Any passer-by may light it and the parish will be obliged. Nobody has obliged it in some time.
the_lampmans_brazier.completion: The planks caught. From the brazier I could see the last lit lamp behind me, and the road ahead as far as the firelight went.

requirements.text: Two planks. There are two in the car in the wood
A fire stone. The car in the wood has one

before_the_bell.name: Before the Bell
before_the_bell.description: Julie's garden book says white water roses do better wild than in the cellar: at Sallow Bottom, on the water, below the jetty. Mrs Allen's cottage is the nearest door to it. Three is plenty. It says she never learned what happens after the bell.
before_the_bell.completion: Three, picked in daylight. They're cold in the hand, like something from a cellar, though they grew in the sun.
before_the_bell.returnTo: Julie's garden book, by the barrel in her yard

requirements.text: White water roses, below the jetty at Sallow Bottom

rose_and_stone.name: Rose and Stone
rose_and_stone.description: The turned-down page in Julie's book: rock breaks to stone at the bench. Stone, a vial of water and a white water rose make Stone Skin. She writes that one should be kept by the door, and that the dog will want to see it. She doesn't say why a dog would.
rose_and_stone.completion: The dog looked at it for some time. Then it told me where the next two things on the shelf used to be.
rose_and_stone.returnTo: the dog, on Julie's step, by day

requirements.text: A Stone Skin potion, made at the kitchen bench, for the dog

stood_down.name: Stood Down
stood_down.description: The Company notice by the mine mouth says the Goldskin Mining Co. has stood its quarry gang down: five men. Any man found working Quarry Steps will be paid off. The Steps are the cut face in the foothills above the gang's camp. The pay hatch is open and nobody is behind it.
stood_down.completion: Five pay packets in the pigeonholes, never drawn. In each, in place of wages, a bar of iron or a plank, and a slip that says IN LIEU.
stood_down.returnTo: the Company notice by the mine mouth

requirements.text: Men working Quarry Steps, up the quarry track from the mine

down_at_five.name: Down at Five: 4
down_at_five.description: A cold camp at the foot of Quarry Steps: five dinner tins laid out by the fire, and a tally slate. The slate says five men went up at seven and four came down at five, and that the foreman would see about it. There's no later entry.
down_at_five.completion: At the top, a rock the size of a shed lies across the mouth of an adit. It was placed, not fallen. In the foreman's tin beside it was a gilder's book with one leaf left. Behind the rock someone is working, steadily, with a hand pick.
down_at_five.returnTo: the tally slate at the gang's camp

requirements.text: The top of Quarry Steps, up from the gang's camp

footpath_three.name: Footpath No. 3
footpath_three.description: The parish council has to walk each right of way once a year or it lapses, and nobody has been free. Footpath No. 3 runs from Castle to Lowfield Farm by the Long Hedge, stile to stile. The notice gives it twelve minutes, and longer in the evening.
footpath_three.completion: Stile to stile. It's a good deal shorter than the road, and nothing on it is lit. I entered the date on the fingerpost card. The last date on it is in the same month, and not in this century.
footpath_three.returnTo: the fingerpost at the Lowfield Farm stile

requirements.text: The stile on Footpath No. 3, outside Castle
The stile on Footpath No. 3, by Lowfield Farm

if_found.name: If Found
if_found.description: A walker's haversack, pushed into a hollow tree on Footpath No. 3 to keep it dry. The label says: if found, return to Lost Property, Castle Halt. Finder's due. It was pushed in from the inside of the tree.
if_found.completion: I entered it in the book. The finder's due is the contents, less the notebook, which stays. Hemshade root, water, and a line in the notebook: root and water, rub it on the blade and not the hand.
if_found.returnTo: the lost-property book, on the platform at Castle Halt

requirements.text: A haversack, from the hollow tree on Footpath No. 3
